html:
The Klickitat are a Sahaptin-speaking people of southern Washington, north of the Columbia River around the Klickitat River and the slopes of Mount Adams. The map spells them Kijkitat.

They lived by salmon fishing, root digging and hunting, and after they got horses they became known as far-ranging traders between the coast and the interior plateau. In the 1830s, after epidemics emptied much of the Willamette Valley, some Klickitat moved south into the lands of the Kalapuya.

In the Yakama Treaty of 1855 they were one of the peoples who gave up land and were placed on the reservation of the Yakama Nation, where most of their descendants are enrolled today. See also Klickitat on the modern map.
sum: The Klickitat are a Sahaptin-speaking people of southern Washington, north of the Columbia River around the Klickitat River and the slopes of Mount Adams. The map spells them Kijkitat.
